THE PROOF PROBLEM

Everybody has to
take your word for it.

The people choosing who gets the job. The people paying for it. The tradesperson deciding where to work next. Three different decisions, and not one of them is made by somebody who has seen you work.

The difference is out on your projects. It is in the call your PM made when the drawings were wrong. The problem you found before it became the owner's problem. The work you stood behind after the invoice was paid.

None of that leaves the site. We bring it back, and put it where the decision gets made.

Common problems we see

You have finished a dozen projects and the only record is photos on a superintendent's phone.

02

03

WHAT YOU GET

One job, three pieces, one link.

01

The project film.

Two to three minutes. The job told by the people who ran it and the client it was built for. Built for the pre-qual package and the bid presentation, and it works on your homepage too.

02

The social cuts.

Three captioned social cuts from the same interviews. Before we film we agree the problems the content has to solve, and each cut is built against one of them.

03

The written case study.

A written case study on a shareable page that is yours, plus a one-page PDF for the bid package. The project, the problem, what you did and what the client said.

BUILT AROUND YOUR JOB

A plan, a day, and we handle the rest.

You are running a job, not a production. One agreed day on site captures the work as it stands; the interviews carry the story of the whole project.

01

We plan it before we film it.

We agree the story angle and the problems the content has to solve before a camera comes out of the case. Every deliverable is mapped to one of them.

02

Interviews tell the whole project.

A camera only sees the day it is there. The story of the whole job, from the drawings to the handover, comes from coordinated interviews with the people who ran it and the client it was built for.

03

The camera captures the agreed site day.

One agreed day on site, around your crew. Access, permissions and releases are sorted first, and we bring cameras, insurance certificates and PPE. Nobody stops working.

04

Then we do the rest.

We edit, write and build the page, then hand it over with a short guide to using it in sales. You approve it once, in one place.

THE DEADLINE

A finished building is just a building.

The proof is the work, and the work only exists while it is happening. Once the site demobilizes, no version of this can be recovered. Not at any price, not by anyone.

If there is a job running right now that you would want a committee to see, that is the one.

TERMS

The things we guarantee.

First cut in fourteen days, or you do not pay.

The first cut is the edited project film, complete enough to review: the story in order, with the interviews and the footage, before your revision round. The fourteen days start the day after the site day, or after the last coordinated interview if that comes later. The clock pauses only while we wait on something only you can give us, such as a signed release, and we tell you when it pauses and when it restarts. If the first cut is late, the project is free: anything you have paid is refunded in full and you keep every file.

Final delivery follows one round of notes.

You send one consolidated set of notes, gathered from everyone who needs a say. We make those changes and deliver the final film, the social cuts, the written case study, the page, the bid PDF and the stills. Final delivery has no fixed date because it depends on when your notes arrive; we confirm the date the day we receive them.

If the footage is not right, we come back on our dime.

If what we got does not hold up, we book another day and cover it. No change order, no mobilization fee.

QUESTIONS

A few things worth knowing.

Who qualifies for the founding price?

Central Ohio contractors with a job we can film and a client or project lead willing to be interviewed about it. The project-fit call is where we find that out together.

What happens on the project-fit call?

You tell us about the job. We tell you straight whether it is a fit, recommend a story angle, and set out exactly what would be filmed, who would be interviewed and what you would get. You leave with that whether or not you go ahead.

Does one day cover the whole project?

The camera covers one agreed day on site: the work as it stands, the crew, the details. The story of the whole project comes from the interviews, with the people who ran it and the client it was built for. That is how a two to three minute film covers a job that ran for a year.

What counts as the first cut?

The edited project film, complete enough to review: the story in order, with the interviews and the footage, before your revision round. The social cuts, the written case study, the page, the bid PDF and the stills follow with final delivery.

When does the fourteen day clock start, and what pauses it?

It starts the day after the site day, or after the last coordinated interview if that is later. It pauses only while we wait on something only you can give us, such as a signed release or an answer we need for the edit, and we tell you when it pauses and when it restarts.

What happens if the first cut is late?

The project is free. Anything you have already paid is refunded in full, and you keep every file we have made.

What is a consolidated revision round?

One set of notes, gathered from everyone who needs a say, sent to us in one place. We make those changes and deliver the final files.

What about ongoing work?

We talk about it after the first story, once we both know it is a good fit. The founding package stands on its own.

What if the project is confidential?

Then it runs as work for hire. Delivered into your systems and never shown publicly, to named recipients only. Same price.

What do you need from my client?

Twenty minutes on camera and a release. We handle the ask if you would rather we did.

What if the weather turns?

We reschedule at no charge and the clock starts from the new date.

Do we own the footage?

Yes. Your organized raw footage is part of the package.

The hard part
is already done.

You built it. You solved the problems on site. The only thing missing is proof that it happened.
